🛑 Requirement: Update the Debian repository architecture lists before adding this target.

The production deployment imports every generated .deb into every configured distribution before creating the GitHub release (.github/workflows/deployment.yml:416-418). All Architectures entries in script/distributions omit s390x, so importing the new package will fail and block the release for all architectures. Add s390x to each distribution's architecture list alongside this build target.

🛑 Requirement: Add license embedding for the new release platform.

The pre-build hook generates internal/licenses/embed/linux-s390x, but there is no embed_linux_s390x.go, and embed_default.go still selects its empty filesystem for linux/s390x. Consequently, the official s390x binary's gh licenses command will print "License information is only available in official release builds." instead of the bundled third-party notices. Add the platform-specific embed file and placeholder, and exclude linux/s390x from the fallback build constraint, as for the other Linux release architectures.

Thanks for your pull request! While it doesn't meet all of our standard requirements, it appears to be a small, focused contribution and has been routed to the team for review.

**Note:** We still encourage linking to an issue with the `help wanted` label when possible, as it helps us prioritize and track contributions.

### 🟡 Changes recommended The new s390x target would block releases because Debian distribution architecture lists omit it, and its official binary lacks embedded third-party license notices.

What changed in this PR Adds Linux s390x release support for GitHub CLI users on IBM Z and LinuxONE through the existing GoReleaser pipeline. **Changes:** - Adds `s390x` to the Linux build architectures, retaining `CGO_ENABLED=0`. - Uses existing packaging rules to generate a tarball, Debian package, and RPM for the new target. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `.goreleaser.yml` | Adds s390x to the Linux release targets without changing macOS or Windows targets. |
